tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

1	# Security review brief (read fully before starting)
2	
3	Project: OpenZeppelin contracts for Stylus (Rust), being migrated to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 on Rust
4	1.91.0. The `bench` branch already contains the migrated contracts crate: it compiles, clippy is
5	clean with `-D warnings`, and all 632 unit tests pass (`cargo +1.91.0 nextest run -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib`).
6	
7	Your worktree is given in your task; it is based on `bench`. Run every cargo and git command in it.
8	Use the 1.91.0 toolchain. The checks: `cargo +1.91.0 nextest run -p <crate> --lib`,
9	`cargo +1.91.0 clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
10	`cargo +nightly-2025-08-01 fmt -p <crate> -- --check`.
11	
12	## Goals (from the project owner, verbatim intent)
13	1. Full security review of the code in your scope.
14	2. Look for what the reports in audits/ missed.
15	3. List the invariants of each contract, then try to break each one.
16	4. Describe every finding: what breaks, how to trigger it, the impact, and the severity.
17	5. For each NEW bug: commit a FAILING proof-of-concept test first, then the fix in a SEPARATE commit.
18	   The PoC commit must fail (show the failing output in your report); the fix commit makes it pass.
19	6. Do not trust audits/. Check every finding the audits mark as resolved (the audit review is
20	   already done; see below) and fix the ones that are only partly fixed or not fixed, when they
21	   are real issues in the code.
22	7. Do not use mutation testing or formal verification.
23	
24	## Known starting points (already verified by reading the v0.3.0 code)
25	Full table: /tmp/bench/notes/audit-findings.md. Items that are NOT really fixed in v0.3.0, which
26	you must re-verify on the migrated code and fix if still real:
27	- v0.3.0 H-01 (PARTIAL): Baby Jubjub generator is not in the prime-order subgroup
28	  (lib/crypto/src/curve/te/instance/baby_jubjub.rs:15-17). Bandersnatch and Jubjub were fixed.
29	- v0.3.0 L-03 (PARTIAL): the UUPS version check can never tell implementations apart: it compares
30	  against a fixed library constant (contracts/src/proxy/utils/uups_upgradeable.rs:54, 434-436,
31	  495-504).
32	- v0.2.0 L-09 (PARTIAL): Uint::eq still exits early (lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:181-188).
33	- v0.2.0 N-01 (NOT FIXED, low): verify_multi_proof and verify_with_builder lack #[must_use]
34	  (lib/crypto/src/merkle.rs:59, 128, 181).
35	- v0.1.0 L-03 (PARTIAL): transfer_from spends the allowance before checking the recipient
36	  (contracts/src/token/erc20/mod.rs; matches Solidity's order, gas only).
37	- Observation: EdDSA signing uses variable-time scalar multiplication with secret scalars
38	  (lib/crypto/src/curve/te/mod.rs:66-96). Assess whether it is reachable in an on-chain
39	  contract or only off-chain, and document the answer.
40	- Ignored tests that describe behaviour the code does not have (investigate each: real bug, or a
41	  wrong test). Do not simply un-ignore a test whose expectation is unmet:
42	  - contracts/src/token/erc721/extensions/wrapper.rs: deposit_for_reverts_when_unsupported_token
43	    (deposit_for never returns UnsupportedToken).
44	  - contracts/src/token/erc20/extensions/wrapper.rs: recover_reverts_when_invalid_underlying
45	    (_recover reports the wrapper's own address in ERC20InvalidUnderlying, the test expects the
46	    underlying token's).
47	  - contracts/src/proxy/beacon/upgradeable.rs (or erc1967/utils.rs): the test
48	    upgrade_beacon_to_and_call_with_beacon_returning_invalid_implementation (TestVM does not roll
49	    back storage on a failed call; check whether the library relies on rollback).
50	  Find every other #[ignore] in your scope (grep) and classify it the same way.
51	
52	## Test-harness facts you need
53	- stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM: `TestVM::default()`, `T::from(&vm)`, `vm.set_sender`, `vm.set_value`,
54	  `vm.set_block_timestamp`, `vm.set_chain_id`, `vm.set_balance`, `vm.get_emitted_logs()`,
55	  `vm.mock_call(addr, data, result)`, `vm.mock_delegate_call`, `vm.mock_static_call`,
56	  `vm.set_code(addr, code)`. Mock return data is ONE shared buffer, so register the mock right
57	  before the call that needs it.
58	- TestVM does not record calls, and a call that matches no mock still succeeds (returns the last
59	  mocked data). Tests that depend on a call failing must mock the failure explicitly.
60	- Shared helpers: contracts/src/test_utils.rs (ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE).
61	- proptest is available (dev-dependency of lib/crypto; add it to contracts dev-dependencies
62	  through the workspace if you need it: `proptest.workspace = true`).
63	
64	## How to work
65	- Start with the invariants: for each contract in your scope, write the invariants down (what must
66	  always hold: balances sum to total supply, a role admin can grant, a proof verifies only the
67	  leaves it commits to, a proxy only delegates to an implementation with code, and so on). Keep
68	  them in your notes file.
69	- Then attack each invariant: read the code paths that change the state, look for missing checks,
70	  wrong order of effects and interactions (reentrancy through the SDK call model, the TestVM
71	  return-data quirk does not apply to the chain), integer rounding and overflow, signature
72	  malleability and replay, unchecked external return values, storage-layout assumptions, and
73	  access-control gaps. Use tests (TestVM and proptest) to confirm.
74	- For each suspected bug: (1) write a PoC test that FAILS on the current code, make a commit with
75	  message `test(security): PoC for <id>` containing only the test; run the test to show it fails;
76	  (2) write the fix in a separate commit `fix(security): <short title>`; the PoC then passes.
77	  Never commit a PoC that you have not seen fail.
78	- A finding that is not a bug (the code is correct, the test was wrong, or the behaviour is by
79	  design) gets a note in your report with the reasoning and evidence, and no commit.
80	- Keep public ABI and behaviour unless a fix requires a change; document any API change in the
81	  report (the upgrade guide needs it).
82	
83	## Commit rules
84	- Message style: `test(security): ...`, `fix(security): ...`, `docs(security): ...`.
85	- End each commit message with only: Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
86	- Do not push. Do not switch branches. Do not touch other worktrees.
87	
88	## Output
89	Write your findings to the notes file named in your task, one entry per finding, with these fields:
90	- ID (SEC-<area>-<n>), title, severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Informational) and why,
91	- where (file:line), what breaks, how to trigger it (the PoC test name), impact,
92	- status: NEW (not in audits/) or EXISTING (the audit finding ID), fix commit or "no change".
93	Also list every invariant you wrote down, and the outcome of each attack (broken with PoC,
94	held with the reason, or not tested with the reason).
95	
96	Final message (at most 40 lines): the counts by severity, the finding IDs with their fix commits,
97	the PoC names, the test counts before and after, and anything you could not finish.

content.text: I'll start by reading the security brief and the audit findings table.

content.content:
1	# Security review brief (read fully before starting)
2	
3	Project: OpenZeppelin contracts for Stylus (Rust), being migrated to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 on Rust
4	1.91.0. The `bench` branch already contains the migrated contracts crate: it compiles, clippy is
5	clean with `-D warnings`, and all 632 unit tests pass (`cargo +1.91.0 nextest run -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib`).
6	
7	Your worktree is given in your task; it is based on `bench`. Run every cargo and git command in it.
8	Use the 1.91.0 toolchain. The checks: `cargo +1.91.0 nextest run -p <crate> --lib`,
9	`cargo +1.91.0 clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
10	`cargo +nightly-2025-08-01 fmt -p <crate> -- --check`.
11	
12	## Goals (from the project owner, verbatim intent)
13	1. Full security review of the code in your scope.
14	2. Look for what the reports in audits/ missed.
15	3. List the invariants of each contract, then try to break each one.
16	4. Describe every finding: what breaks, how to trigger it, the impact, and the severity.
17	5. For each NEW bug: commit a FAILING proof-of-concept test first, then the fix in a SEPARATE commit.
18	   The PoC commit must fail (show the failing output in your report); the fix commit makes it pass.
19	6. Do not trust audits/. Check every finding the audits mark as resolved (the audit review is
20	   already done; see below) and fix the ones that are only partly fixed or not fixed, when they
21	   are real issues in the code.
22	7. Do not use mutation testing or formal verification.
23	
24	## Known starting points (already verified by reading the v0.3.0 code)
25	Full table: /tmp/bench/notes/audit-findings.md. Items that are NOT really fixed in v0.3.0, which
26	you must re-verify on the migrated code and fix if still real:
27	- v0.3.0 H-01 (PARTIAL): Baby Jubjub generator is not in the prime-order subgroup
28	  (lib/crypto/src/curve/te/instance/baby_jubjub.rs:15-17). Bandersnatch and Jubjub were fixed.
29	- v0.3.0 L-03 (PARTIAL): the UUPS version check can never tell implementations apart: it compares
30	  against a fixed library constant (contracts/src/proxy/utils/uups_upgradeable.rs:54, 434-436,
31	  495-504).
32	- v0.2.0 L-09 (PARTIAL): Uint::eq still exits early (lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:181-188).
33	- v0.2.0 N-01 (NOT FIXED, low): verify_multi_proof and verify_with_builder lack #[must_use]
34	  (lib/crypto/src/merkle.rs:59, 128, 181).
35	- v0.1.0 L-03 (PARTIAL): transfer_from spends the allowance before checking the recipient
36	  (contracts/src/token/erc20/mod.rs; matches Solidity's order, gas only).
37	- Observation: EdDSA signing uses variable-time scalar multiplication with secret scalars
38	  (lib/crypto/src/curve/te/mod.rs:66-96). Assess whether it is reachable in an on-chain
39	  contract or only off-chain, and document the answer.
40	- Ignored tests that describe behaviour the code does not have (investigate each: real bug, or a
41	  wrong test). Do not simply un-ignore a test whose expectation is unmet:
42	  - contracts/src/token/erc721/extensions/wrapper.rs: deposit_for_reverts_when_unsupported_token
43	    (deposit_for never returns UnsupportedToken).
44	  - contracts/src/token/erc20/extensions/wrapper.rs: recover_reverts_when_invalid_underlying
45	    (_recover reports the wrapper's own address in ERC20InvalidUnderlying, the test expects the
46	    underlying token's).
47	  - contracts/src/proxy/beacon/upgradeable.rs (or erc1967/utils.rs): the test
48	    upgrade_beacon_to_and_call_with_beacon_returning_invalid_implementation (TestVM does not roll
49	    back storage on a failed call; check whether the library relies on rollback).
50	  Find every other #[ignore] in your scope (grep) and classify it the same way.
51	
52	## Test-harness facts you need
53	- stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM: `TestVM::default()`, `T::from(&vm)`, `vm.set_sender`, `vm.set_value`,
54	  `vm.set_block_timestamp`, `vm.set_chain_id`, `vm.set_balance`, `vm.get_emitted_logs()`,
55	  `vm.mock_call(addr, data, result)`, `vm.mock_delegate_call`, `vm.mock_static_call`,
56	  `vm.set_code(addr, code)`. Mock return data is ONE shared buffer, so register the mock right
57	  before the call that needs it.
58	- TestVM does not record calls, and a call that matches no mock still succeeds (returns the last
59	  mocked data). Tests that depend on a call failing must mock the failure explicitly.
60	- Shared helpers: contracts/src/test_utils.rs (ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE).
61	- proptest is available (dev-dependency of lib/crypto; add it to contracts dev-dependencies
62	  through the workspace if you need it: `proptest.workspace = true`).
63	
64	## How to work
65	- Start with the invariants: for each contract in your scope, write the invariants down (what must
66	  always hold: balances sum to total supply, a role admin can grant, a proof verifies only the
67	  leaves it commits to, a proxy only delegates to an implementation with code, and so on). Keep
68	  them in your notes file.
69	- Then attack each invariant: read the code paths that change the state, look for missing checks,
70	  wrong order of effects and interactions (reentrancy through the SDK call model, the TestVM
71	  return-data quirk does not apply to the chain), integer rounding and overflow, signature
72	  malleability and replay, unchecked external return values, storage-layout assumptions, and
73	  access-control gaps. Use tests (TestVM and proptest) to confirm.
74	- For each suspected bug: (1) write a PoC test that FAILS on the current code, make a commit with
75	  message `test(security): PoC for <id>` containing only the test; run the test to show it fails;
76	  (2) write the fix in a separate commit `fix(security): <short title>`; the PoC then passes.
77	  Never commit a PoC that you have not seen fail.
78	- A finding that is not a bug (the code is correct, the test was wrong, or the behaviour is by
79	  design) gets a note in your report with the reasoning and evidence, and no commit.
80	- Keep public ABI and behaviour unless a fix requires a change; document any API change in the
81	  report (the upgrade guide needs it).
82	
83	## Commit rules
84	- Message style: `test(security): ...`, `fix(security): ...`, `docs(security): ...`.
85	- End each commit message with only: Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
86	- Do not push. Do not switch branches. Do not touch other worktrees.
87	
88	## Output
89	Write your findings to the notes file named in your task, one entry per finding, with these fields:
90	- ID (SEC-<area>-<n>), title, severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Informational) and why,
91	- where (file:line), what breaks, how to trigger it (the PoC test name), impact,
92	- status: NEW (not in audits/) or EXISTING (the audit finding ID), fix commit or "no change".
93	Also list every invariant you wrote down, and the outcome of each attack (broken with PoC,
94	held with the reason, or not tested with the reason).
95	
96	Final message (at most 40 lines): the counts by severity, the finding IDs with their fix commits,
97	the PoC names, the test counts before and after, and anything you could not finish.

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. - Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. # SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)

Accessors (global -> VM):
  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).

Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
Import paths:
  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error
  stylus_sdk::call::{Call, StaticCallContext}-> in prelude (stylus_sdk::prelude::*)
  stylus_sdk::evm / msg / block / contract   -> removed (use self.vm())

Traits:
  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.

Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }

Decisions taken while fixing the shared core (apply everywhere):
  AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(context: &mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>), target, data)
      builds `let call = Call::new_mutating(context);` FIRST, then `call::delegate_call(context.vm(), call, ...)`.
  AddressUtils::verify_call_result_from_target(context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>, target, result)
  AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr) -> bool          (pub(crate); replaces Address::has_code())
  Erc1967Utils: every fn that reads/writes a slot or emits/gets msg value takes `context` first:
      get_implementation(context), get_admin(context), change_admin(context, new_admin),
      get_beacon(context), upgrade_to_and_call(context, impl, data), upgrade_beacon_to_and_call(context, beacon, data)
  IEip712: `pub trait IEip712: HostAccess` (no #[public], it has associated consts);
      chain_id(&self), contract_address(&self) are methods, not associated fns.
  Interface wrappers from sol_interface!: f(context.vm(), Call::new()/Call::new_mutating(self)/..., args).
      Static calls use Call::new() (no storage borrow needed).
Test fixtures: contracts/src/test_utils.rs exports ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE (const Address).
test(erc1155): cover the receiver acceptance check with mocked calls

The unit tests only used accounts without code, so the acceptance check that
this migration touched (code check, call context, host argument, error
mapping) was exercised by the end-to-end tests alone. `TestVM::set_code` and
`mock_call` make it testable natively: a receiver contract that accepts a
single and a batch transfer, answers with the wrong selector, and reverts with
and without a reason, plus the same check through `Erc1155Supply`. These are
additional tests; none of the migrated ones depends on them.

1	//! Implementation of the ERC-20 token standard.
2	//!
3	//! We have followed general `OpenZeppelin` Contracts guidelines: functions
4	//! revert instead of returning `false` on failure. This behavior is
5	//! nonetheless conventional and does not conflict with the expectations of
6	//! [`Erc20`] applications.
7	use alloc::{vec, vec::Vec};
8	
9	use alloy_primitives::{aliases::B32, Address, U256};
10	use openzeppelin_stylus_proc::interface_id;
11	use stylus_sdk::{
12	    prelude::*,
13	    storage::{StorageMap, StorageU256},
14	    stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError,
15	};
16	
17	use crate::utils::{
18	    introspection::erc165::IErc165,
19	    math::storage::{AddAssignChecked, AddAssignUnchecked, SubAssignUnchecked},
20	};
21	
22	pub mod extensions;
23	pub mod interface;
24	pub mod utils;
25	
26	pub use sol::*;
27	#[cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]
28	mod sol {
29	    use alloy_sol_macro::sol;
30	
31	    sol! {
32	        /// Emitted when `value` tokens are moved from one account (`from`) to
33	        /// another (`to`).
34	        ///
35	        /// Note that `value` may be zero.
36	        #[derive(Debug)]
37	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
38	        event Transfer(address indexed from, address indexed to, uint256 value);
39	        /// Emitted when the allowance of a `spender` for an `owner` is set by a
40	        /// call to `approve`. `value` is the new allowance.
41	        #[derive(Debug)]
42	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
43	        event Approval(address indexed owner, address indexed spender, uint256 value);
44	    }
45	
46	    sol! {
47	        /// Indicates an error related to the current `balance` of `sender`. Used
48	        /// in transfers.
49	        ///
50	        /// * `sender` - Address whose tokens are being transferred.
51	        /// * `balance` - Current balance for the interacting account.
52	        /// * `needed` - Minimum amount required to perform a transfer.
53	        #[derive(Debug)]
54	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
55	        error ERC20InsufficientBalance(address sender, uint256 balance, uint256 needed);
56	        /// Indicates a failure with the token `sender`. Used in transfers.
57	        ///
58	        /// * `sender` - Address whose tokens are being transferred.
59	        #[derive(Debug)]
60	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
61	        error ERC20InvalidSender(address sender);
62	        /// Indicates a failure with the token `receiver`. Used in transfers.
63	        ///
64	        /// * `receiver` - Address to which the tokens are being transferred.
65	        #[derive(Debug)]
66	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
67	        error ERC20InvalidReceiver(address receiver);
68	        /// Indicates a failure with the `spender`’s `allowance`. Used in
69	        /// transfers.
70	        ///
71	        /// * `spender` - Address that may be allowed to operate on tokens without
72	        /// being their owner.
73	        /// * `allowance` - Amount of tokens a `spender` is allowed to operate
74	        /// with.
75	        /// * `needed` - Minimum amount required to perform a transfer.
76	        #[derive(Debug)]
77	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
78	        error ERC20InsufficientAllowance(address spender, uint256 allowance, uint256 needed);
79	        /// Indicates a failure with the `spender` to be approved. Used in
80	        /// approvals.
81	        ///
82	        /// * `spender` - Address that may be allowed to operate on tokens without
83	        /// being their owner.
84	        #[derive(Debug)]
85	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
86	        error ERC20InvalidSpender(address spender);

326	    /// Sets a `value` number of tokens as the allowance of `spender` over the
327	    /// caller's tokens.
328	    ///
329	    /// Returns a boolean value indicating whether the operation succeeded.
330	    /// # Arguments
331	    ///
332	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
333	    /// * `owner` - Account that owns the tokens.
334	    /// * `spender` - Account that will spend the tokens.
335	    /// * `emit_event` - Emit an [`Approval`] event flag.
336	    ///
337	    /// # Errors
338	    ///
339	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSpender`] - If the `spender` address is
340	    ///   [`Address::ZERO`].
341	    ///
342	    /// # Events
343	    ///
344	    /// * [`Approval`].
345	    fn _approve(
346	        &mut self,
347	        owner: Address,
348	        spender: Address,
349	        value: U256,
350	        emit_event: bool,
351	    ) -> Result<bool, Error> {
352	        if owner.is_zero() {
353	            return Err(Error::InvalidApprover(ERC20InvalidApprover {
354	                approver: Address::ZERO,
355	            }));
356	        }
357	
358	        if spender.is_zero() {
359	            return Err(Error::InvalidSpender(ERC20InvalidSpender {
360	                spender: Address::ZERO,
361	            }));
362	        }
363	
364	        self.allowances.setter(owner).insert(spender, value);
365	        if emit_event {
366	            self.vm().log(Approval { owner, spender, value });
367	        }
368	        Ok(true)
369	    }

371	    /// Internal implementation of transferring tokens between two accounts.
372	    ///
373	    /// # Arguments
374	    ///
375	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
376	    /// * `from` - Account to transfer tokens from.
377	    /// * `to` - Account to transfer tokens to.
378	    /// * `value` - The number of tokens to transfer.
379	    ///
380	    /// # Errors
381	    ///
382	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSender`] - If the `from` address is [`Address::ZERO`].
383	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If the `to` address is [`Address::ZERO`].
384	    /// * [`Error::InsufficientBalance`] - If the `from` address doesn't have
385	    ///   enough tokens.
386	    ///
387	    /// # Events
388	    ///
389	    /// * [`Transfer`].
390	    fn _transfer(
391	        &mut self,
392	        from: Address,
393	        to: Address,
394	        value: U256,
395	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
396	        if from.is_zero() {
397	            return Err(Error::InvalidSender(ERC20InvalidSender {
398	                sender: Address::ZERO,
399	            }));
400	        }
401	        if to.is_zero() {
402	            return Err(Error::InvalidReceiver(ERC20InvalidReceiver {
403	                receiver: Address::ZERO,
404	            }));
405	        }
406	
407	        self._update(from, to, value)?;
408	
409	        Ok(())
410	    }
411	
412	    /// Creates a `value` amount of tokens and assigns them to `account`,
413	    /// by transferring it from [`Address::ZERO`].
414	    ///
415	    /// # Errors
416	    ///
417	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If the `account` address is
418	    ///   [`Address::ZERO`].
419	    ///
420	    /// # Events
421	    ///
422	    /// * [`Transfer`].
423	    ///
424	    /// # Panics
425	    ///
426	    /// * If `total_supply` exceeds [`U256::MAX`].
427	    pub fn _mint(
428	        &mut self,
429	        account: Address,
430	        value: U256,
431	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
432	        if account.is_zero() {
433	            return Err(Error::InvalidReceiver(ERC20InvalidReceiver {
434	                receiver: Address::ZERO,
435	            }));
436	        }
437	        self._update(Address::ZERO, account, value)
438	    }
439	
440	    /// Transfers a `value` amount of tokens from `from` to `to`, or
441	    /// alternatively mints (or burns) if `from` (or `to`) is the zero address.
442	    ///
443	    /// All customizations to transfers, mints, and burns should be done by
444	    /// using this function.
445	    ///
446	    /// # Arguments
447	    ///
448	    /// * `from` - Owner's address.
449	    /// * `to` - Recipient's address.
450	    /// * `value` - Amount to be transferred.
451	    ///
452	    /// # Errors
453	    ///
454	    /// * [`Error::InsufficientBalance`] - If the `from` address doesn't have
455	    ///   enough tokens.
456	    ///
457	    /// # Events
458	    ///
459	    /// * [`Transfer`].
460	    ///
461	    /// # Panics
462	    ///
463	    /// * If `total_supply` exceeds [`U256::MAX`]. It may happen during `mint`
464	    ///   operation.
465	    pub fn _update(
466	        &mut self,
467	        from: Address,
468	        to: Address,
469	        value: U256,
470	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
471	        if from.is_zero() {
472	            // Mint operation. Overflow check required: the rest of the code
473	            // assumes that `total_supply` never overflows.
474	            self.total_supply.add_assign_checked(
475	                value,
476	                "should not exceed `U256::MAX` for `total_supply`",
477	            );
478	        } else {
479	            let from_balance = self.balances.get(from);
480	            if from_balance < value {
481	                return Err(Error::InsufficientBalance(
482	                    ERC20InsufficientBalance {
483	                        sender: from,
484	                        balance: from_balance,
485	                        needed: value,
486	                    },
487	                ));
488	            }
489	            // Overflow not possible:
490	            // `value` <= `from_balance` <= `total_supply`.
491	            self.balances.setter(from).set(from_balance - value);
492	        }
493	
494	        if to.is_zero() {
495	            // Overflow not possible:
496	            // `value` <= `total_supply` or
497	            // `value` <= `from_balance` <= `total_supply`.
498	            self.total_supply.sub_assign_unchecked(value);
499	        } else {
500	            // Overflow not possible:
501	            // `balance_to` + `value` is at most `total_supply`,
502	            // which fits into a `U256`.
503	            self.balances.setter(to).add_assign_unchecked(value);
504	        }
505	
506	        self.vm().log(Transfer { from, to, value });
507	
508	        Ok(())
509	    }
510	
511	    /// Destroys a `value` amount of tokens from `account`,
512	    /// lowering the total supply.
513	    ///
514	    /// # Arguments
515	    ///
516	    /// * `account` - Owner's address.
517	    /// * `value` - Amount to be burnt.
518	    ///
519	    /// # Errors
520	    ///
521	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSender`] - If the `from` address is [`Address::ZERO`].
522	    /// * [`Error::InsufficientBalance`] - If the `from` address doesn't have
523	    ///   enough tokens.
524	    ///
525	    /// # Events
526	    ///
527	    /// * [`Transfer`].
528	    pub fn _burn(
529	        &mut self,
530	        account: Address,
531	        value: U256,
532	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
533	        if account == Address::ZERO {
534	            return Err(Error::InvalidSender(ERC20InvalidSender {
535	                sender: Address::ZERO,
536	            }));
537	        }
538	        self._update(account, Address::ZERO, value)
539	    }
540	
541	    /// Updates `owner`'s allowance for `spender` based on spent `value`.
542	    ///
543	    /// Does not update the allowance value in the case of infinite allowance.
544	    ///
545	    /// # Arguments
546	    ///
547	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
548	    /// * `owner` - Account to transfer tokens from.
549	    /// * `to` - Account to transfer tokens to.
550	    /// * `value` - The number of tokens to transfer.
551	    ///
552	    /// # Errors
553	    ///
554	    /// * [`Error::InsufficientAllowance`] - If not enough allowance is
555	    ///   available.
556	    ///
557	    /// # Events
558	    ///
559	    /// * [`Approval`].
560	    pub fn _spend_allowance(
561	        &mut self,
562	        owner: Address,
563	        spender: Address,
564	        value: U256,
565	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
566	        let current_allowance = self.allowance(owner, spender);
567	        if current_allowance != U256::MAX {
568	            if current_allowance < value {
569	                return Err(Error::InsufficientAllowance(
570	                    ERC20InsufficientAllowance {
571	                        spender,
572	                        allowance: current_allowance,
573	                        needed: value,
574	                    },
575	                ));
576	            }
577	
578	            self._approve(owner, spender, current_allowance - value, false)?;
579	        }
580	
581	        Ok(())
582	    }
583	}

1	//! Permit Contract.
2	//!
3	//! Extension of the ERC-20 standard allowing approvals to be made
4	//! via signatures, as defined in the [ERC].
5	//!
6	//! Adds the `permit` method, which can be used to change an account’s
7	//! ERC20 allowance (see [`crate::token::erc20::IErc20::allowance`])
8	//! by presenting a message signed by the account.
9	//! By not relying on [`erc20::IErc20::approve`],
10	//! the token holder account doesn’t need to send a transaction,
11	//! and thus is not required to hold Ether at all.
12	//!
13	//! [ERC]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612
14	
15	use alloc::{vec, vec::Vec};
16	
17	use alloy_primitives::{aliases::B32, keccak256, Address, B256, U256, U8};
18	use alloy_sol_types::SolType;
19	use stylus_sdk::{
20	    function_selector, prelude::*, stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError,
21	};
22	
23	use crate::{
24	    token::erc20::{self, Erc20},
25	    utils::{
26	        cryptography::eip712::IEip712,
27	        nonces::{INonces, Nonces},
28	        precompiles::{
29	            primitives::ecrecover::{
30	                self, ECDSAInvalidSignature, ECDSAInvalidSignatureS,
31	            },
32	            Precompiles,
33	        },
34	    },
35	};
36	
37	const PERMIT_TYPEHASH: [u8; 32] =
38	    keccak_const::Keccak256::new()
39	        .update(b"Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)")
40	        .finalize();
41	
42	pub use sol::*;
43	#[cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]
44	mod sol {
45	    use alloy_sol_macro::sol;
46	
47	    pub(crate) type StructHashTuple = sol! {
48	        tuple(bytes32, address, address, uint256, uint256, uint256)
49	    };
50	
51	    sol! {
52	        /// Indicates an error related to the fact that
53	        /// permit deadline has expired.
54	        #[derive(Debug)]
55	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
56	        error ERC2612ExpiredSignature(uint256 deadline);
57	
58	        /// Indicates an error related to the issue about mismatched signature.
59	        #[derive(Debug)]
60	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
61	        error ERC2612InvalidSigner(address signer, address owner);
62	    }
63	}
64	
65	/// A Permit error.
66	#[derive(SolidityError, Debug)]
67	pub enum Error {
68	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that
69	    /// permit deadline has expired.
70	    ExpiredSignature(ERC2612ExpiredSignature),
71	    /// Indicates an error related to the issue about mismatched signature.
72	    InvalidSigner(ERC2612InvalidSigner),
73	    /// Indicates an error related to the current balance of `sender`. Used in
74	    /// transfers.
75	    InsufficientBalance(erc20::ERC20InsufficientBalance),
76	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `sender`. Used in transfers.
77	    InvalidSender(erc20::ERC20InvalidSender),
78	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `receiver`. Used in transfers.
79	    InvalidReceiver(erc20::ERC20InvalidReceiver),
80	    /// Indicates a failure with the `spender`’s `allowance`. Used in
81	    /// transfers.
82	    InsufficientAllowance(erc20::ERC20InsufficientAllowance),
83	    /// Indicates a failure with the `spender` to be approved. Used in
84	    /// approvals.
85	    InvalidSpender(erc20::ERC20InvalidSpender),
86	    /// Indicates a failure with the `approver` of a token to be approved. Used
87	    /// in approvals. approver Address initiating an approval operation.
88	    InvalidApprover(erc20::ERC20InvalidApprover),
89	    /// The signature derives the [`Address::ZERO`].
90	    InvalidSignature(ECDSAInvalidSignature),
91	    /// The signature has an `S` value that is in the upper half order.
92	    InvalidSignatureS(ECDSAInvalidSignatureS),
93	}
94	
95	impl From<erc20::Error> for Error {
96	    fn from(value: erc20::Error) -> Self {
97	        match value {
98	            erc20::Error::InsufficientBalance(e) => {
99	                Error::InsufficientBalance(e)
100	            }
101	            erc20::Error::InvalidSender(e) => Error::InvalidSender(e),
102	            erc20::Error::InvalidReceiver(e) => Error::InvalidReceiver(e),
103	            erc20::Error::InsufficientAllowance(e) => {
104	                Error::InsufficientAllowance(e)
105	            }

145	pub trait IErc20Permit: INonces {
146	    /// The error type associated to this interface.

149	    // Calculated manually to include [`INonces::nonces`].
150	    /// Solidity interface id associated with [`IErc20Permit`] trait.

152	    #[must_use]
153	    fn interface_id() -> B32
154	    where
155	        Self: Sized,
156	    {
157	        B32::new(function_selector!("DOMAIN_SEPARATOR",))
158	            ^ B32::new(function_selector!("nonces", Address,))
159	            ^ B32::new(function_selector!(
160	                "permit", Address, Address, U256, U256, U8, B256, B256

179	    ///

214	        v: u8,

224	        self.eip712.domain_separator_v4()
225	    }

227	    /// See [`IErc20Permit::permit`].
228	    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments, clippy::missing_errors_doc)]
229	    pub fn permit(
230	        &mut self,
231	        owner: Address,
232	        spender: Address,
233	        value: U256,
234	        deadline: U256,
235	        v: u8,
236	        r: B256,
237	        s: B256,
238	        erc20: &mut Erc20,
239	        nonces: &mut Nonces,
240	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
241	        if U256::from(self.vm().block_timestamp()) > deadline {
242	            return Err(ERC2612ExpiredSignature { deadline }.into());
243	        }
244	
245	        let struct_hash = keccak256(StructHashTuple::abi_encode(&(
246	            PERMIT_TYPEHASH,
247	            owner,
248	            spender,
249	            value,
250	            nonces.use_nonce(owner),
251	            deadline,
252	        )));
253	
254	        let hash: B256 = self.eip712.hash_typed_data_v4(struct_hash);
255	
256	        let signer: Address = self.ec_recover(hash, v, r, s)?;
257	
258	        if signer != owner {
259	            return Err(ERC2612InvalidSigner { signer, owner }.into());
260	        }
261	
262	        erc20._approve(owner, spender, value, true)?;
263	
264	        Ok(())
265	    }
266	}

18	    /// This module provides the cryptographic primitives needed for the

32	/// Trait providing access to Arbitrum precompiles for Stylus contracts.
33	///
34	/// This trait wraps complex precompile invocations to provide a clean,
35	/// ergonomic interface for calling Arbitrum's built-in cryptographic functions
36	/// and utilities from within Stylus smart contracts.
37	///
38	/// Precompiles are pre-deployed contracts at fixed addresses that implement
39	/// commonly used cryptographic operations and other utilities. They execute
40	/// natively in the Arbitrum runtime for better performance compared to
41	/// implementing these operations in contract code.
42	///
43	/// See: <https://docs.arbitrum.io/build-decentralized-apps/precompiles/overview>
44	///
45	/// # Usage
46	///
47	/// Implement this trait for your contract storage type to gain access to
48	/// precompile functionality:
49	///
50	/// ```rust,ignore
51	/// use openzeppelin_stylus::utils::precompiles::Precompiles;
52	///
53	/// #[storage]
54	/// #[entrypoint]
55	/// struct MyContract {
56	///     // your fields...
57	/// }
58	///
59	/// // The `Precompiles` trait is automatically implemented for all
60	/// // contracts annotated with `#[entrypoint]` or that implement
61	/// // `stylus_sdk::prelude::TopLevelStorage`, as long as they give access to
62	/// // the host through `stylus_sdk::prelude::HostAccess` (which `#[storage]`
63	/// // already provides).
64	///
65	/// #[public]
66	/// impl MyContract {
67	///     fn verify_signature(&mut self, msg_hash: B256, sig: (u8, B256, B256)) -> Result<Address, Error> {
68	///         let (v, r, s) = sig;
69	///         self.ec_recover(msg_hash, v, r, s)
70	///     }
71	/// }
72	/// ```
73	///
74	/// # Error Handling
75	///
76	/// Precompile methods return `Result` types to handle both invalid inputs and
77	/// precompile execution failures. Always handle these errors appropriately
78	/// in your contract logic.
79	pub trait Precompiles: TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM> {
80	    /// Recovers the address that signed a hashed message (`hash`) using an
81	    /// ECDSA signature (v, r, s).
82	    ///
83	    /// Wrapper around the `ecRecover` precompile.
84	    ///
85	    /// # Arguments
86	    ///
87	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
88	    /// * `hash` - Hash of the message.
89	    /// * `v` - `v` value from the signature.
90	    /// * `r` - `r` value from the signature.
91	    /// * `s` - `s` value from the signature.
92	    ///
93	    /// # Errors
94	    ///
95	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSignatureS`] - If the `s` value is grater than
96	    ///   [`primitives::ecrecover::SIGNATURE_S_UPPER_BOUND`].
97	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSignature`] - If the recovered address is
98	    ///   [`Address::ZERO`].
99	    ///
100	    /// # Panics
101	    ///
102	    /// * If the `ecRecover` precompile fails to execute.
103	    fn ec_recover(
104	        &self,
105	        hash: B256,
106	        v: u8,
107	        r: B256,
108	        s: B256,
109	    ) -> Result<Address, Error>;
110	
111	    /// Performs signature verifications in the `secp256r1` elliptic curve.
112	    ///
113	    /// Wrapper around the `P256VERIFY` precompile introduced in [RIP-7212].
114	    ///
115	    /// [RIP-7212]: https://github.com/ethereum/RIPs/blob/723155c3d86427412b5bc0f98ad1e4791ea7347f/RIPS/rip-7212.md
116	    ///
117	    /// # Arguments
118	    ///
119	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
120	    /// * `hash` - Signed data hash.
121	    /// * `r` - `r` component of the signature.
122	    /// * `s` - `s` component of the signature.
123	    /// * `x` - `x` coordinate of the public key.
124	    /// * `y` - `y` coordinate of the public key.
125	    fn p256_verify(
126	        &self,
127	        hash: B256,
128	        r: B256,
129	        s: B256,
130	        x: B256,
131	        y: B256,
132	    ) -> bool;
133	}
134	
135	impl<T: TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>> Precompiles for T {
136	    fn ec_recover(
137	        &self,
138	        hash: B256,
139	        v: u8,
140	        r: B256,
141	        s: B256,
142	    ) -> Result<Address, Error> {
143	        recover(self, hash, v, r, s)
144	    }
145	
146	    fn p256_verify(
147	        &self,
148	        hash: B256,
149	        r: B256,
150	        s: B256,
151	        x: B256,
152	        y: B256,
153	    ) -> bool {
154	        p256_verify(self, hash, r, s, x, y)
155	    }
156	}

1	//! Implementation of the ERC-3156 Flash loans extension, as defined in
2	//! [ERC-3156].
3	//!
4	//! Adds the [`IErc3156FlashLender::flash_loan`] method, which provides flash
5	//! loan support at the token level. By default there is no fee, but this can be
6	//! changed by overriding [`IErc3156FlashLender::flash_loan`].
7	//!
8	//! NOTE: When this extension is used along with the
9	//! [`crate::token::erc20::extensions::Capped`] extension,
10	//! [`IErc3156FlashLender::max_flash_loan`] will not correctly reflect the
11	//! maximum that can be flash minted. We recommend overriding
12	//! [`IErc3156FlashLender::max_flash_loan`] so that it correctly reflects the
13	//! supply cap.
14	//!
15	//! [ERC-3156]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3156
16	
17	// TODO: once ERC20Votes is implemented, include it in the comment above next to
18	// ERC20Capped.
19	
20	use alloc::{vec, vec::Vec};
21	
22	use alloy_primitives::{Address, U256};
23	use openzeppelin_stylus_proc::interface_id;
24	use stylus_sdk::{
25	    abi::Bytes,
26	    prelude::*,
27	    storage::{StorageAddress, StorageU256},
28	    stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError,
29	};

32	    token::erc20::{self, Erc20, IErc20},
33	    utils::address::AddressUtils,
34	};

36	/// The expected value returned from [`IERC3156FlashBorrower::on_flash_loan`].
37	pub const BORROWER_CALLBACK_VALUE: [u8; 32] = keccak_const::Keccak256::new()
38	    .update("ERC3156FlashBorrower.onFlashLoan".as_bytes())
39	    .finalize();
40	
41	pub use sol::*;
42	mod sol {
43	    #![cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]
44	    use alloy_sol_macro::sol;
45	
46	    sol! {
47	        /// Indicate that the loan token is not supported or valid.
48	        ///
49	        /// * `token` - Address of the unsupported token.
50	        #[derive(Debug)]
51	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
52	        error ERC3156UnsupportedToken(address token);
53	
54	        /// Indicate an error related to the loan value exceeding the maximum.
55	        ///
56	        /// * `max_loan` - Maximum loan value.
57	        #[derive(Debug)]
58	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
59	        error ERC3156ExceededMaxLoan(uint256 max_loan);
60	
61	        /// Indicate that the receiver of a flashloan is not a valid [`IERC3156FlashBorrower::on_flash_loan`] implementer.
62	        ///
63	        /// * `receiver` - Address to which tokens are being transferred.
64	        #[derive(Debug)]
65	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
66	        error ERC3156InvalidReceiver(address receiver);
67	    }
68	}

70	/// An [`Erc20FlashMint`] extension error.
71	#[derive(SolidityError, Debug)]
72	pub enum Error {
73	    /// Indicate that the loan token is not supported or valid.
74	    UnsupportedToken(ERC3156UnsupportedToken),
75	    /// Indicate an error related to the loan value exceeding the maximum.
76	    ExceededMaxLoan(ERC3156ExceededMaxLoan),
77	    /// Indicate that the receiver of a flashloan is not a valid
78	    /// [`IERC3156FlashBorrower::on_flash_loan`] implementer.
79	    ERC3156InvalidReceiver(ERC3156InvalidReceiver),
80	    /// Indicates an error related to the current balance of `sender`. Used in
81	    /// transfers.
82	    InsufficientBalance(erc20::ERC20InsufficientBalance),
83	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `sender`. Used in transfers.
84	    InvalidSender(erc20::ERC20InvalidSender),
85	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `receiver`. Used in transfers.
86	    InvalidReceiver(erc20::ERC20InvalidReceiver),
87	    /// Indicates a failure with the `spender`’s `allowance`. Used in
88	    /// transfers.
89	    InsufficientAllowance(erc20::ERC20InsufficientAllowance),
90	    /// Indicates a failure with the `spender` to be approved. Used in
91	    /// approvals.
92	    InvalidSpender(erc20::ERC20InvalidSpender),
93	    /// Indicates a failure with the `approver` of a token to be approved. Used
94	    /// in approvals. approver Address initiating an approval operation.
95	    InvalidApprover(erc20::ERC20InvalidApprover),
96	}
97	
98	impl From<erc20::Error> for Error {
99	    fn from(value: erc20::Error) -> Self {
100	        match value {
101	            erc20::Error::InsufficientBalance(e) => {
102	                Error::InsufficientBalance(e)
103	            }
104	            erc20::Error::InvalidSender(e) => Error::InvalidSender(e),
105	            erc20::Error::InvalidReceiver(e) => Error::InvalidReceiver(e),
106	            erc20::Error::InsufficientAllowance(e) => {
107	                Error::InsufficientAllowance(e)
108	            }
109	            erc20::Error::InvalidSpender(e) => Error::InvalidSpender(e),
110	            erc20::Error::InvalidApprover(e) => Error::InvalidApprover(e),
111	        }
112	    }
113	}
114	
115	impl MethodError for Error {
116	    fn encode(self) -> alloc::vec::Vec<u8> {
117	        self.into()
118	    }
119	}

121	pub use borrower::IERC3156FlashBorrower;
122	mod borrower {
123	    #![allow(missing_docs)]
124	    #![cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]
125	    use alloc::vec;
126	
127	    use stylus_sdk::prelude::sol_interface;
128	
129	    sol_interface! {
130	        /// Interface of the ERC-3156 Flash Borrower, as defined in [ERC-3156].
131	        ///
132	        /// [ERC-3156]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3156
133	        interface IERC3156FlashBorrower {
134	            /// Receives a flash loan.
135	            ///
136	            /// To indicate successful handling of the flash loan, this function should return
137	            /// the `keccak256` hash of "ERC3156FlashBorrower.onFlashLoan".
138	            ///
139	            /// # Arguments
140	            ///
141	            /// * `initiator` - The initiator of the flash loan.
142	            /// * `token` - The token to be flash loaned.
143	            /// * `amount` - The amount of tokens lent.
144	            /// * `fee` - The additional amount of tokens to repay.
145	            /// * `data` - Arbitrary data structure, intended to contain user-defined parameters.
146	            #[allow(missing_docs)]
147	            #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
148	            function onFlashLoan(
149	                address initiator,
150	                address token,
151	                uint256 amount,
152	                uint256 fee,
153	                bytes calldata data
154	            ) external returns (bytes32);
155	        }
156	    }
157	}
158	
159	/// State of an [`Erc20FlashMint`] Contract.
160	#[storage]
161	pub struct Erc20FlashMint {
162	    // TODO: Remove this field once function overriding is possible. For now we
163	    // keep this field `pub`, since this is used to simulate overriding.
164	    /// Fee applied when doing flash loans.
165	    pub flash_fee_value: StorageU256,
166	    // TODO: Remove this field once function overriding is possible. For now we
167	    // keep this field `pub`, since this is used to simulate overriding.
168	    /// Receiver address of the flash fee.
169	    pub flash_fee_receiver_address: StorageAddress,
170	}
171	
172	/// NOTE: Implementation of [`TopLevelStorage`] to be able use `&mut self` when
173	/// calling other contracts and not `&mut (impl TopLevelStorage +
174	/// BorrowMut<Self>)`. Should be fixed in the future by the Stylus team.
175	unsafe impl TopLevelStorage for Erc20FlashMint {}
176	
177	/// Interface of the ERC-3156 Flash Lender, as defined in [ERC-3156].
178	///
179	/// [ERC-3156]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3156
180	#[interface_id]
181	#[public]
182	// The `#[public]` macro adds an undocumented helper method to the trait.
183	#[allow(missing_docs)]
184	pub trait IErc3156FlashLender {
185	    /// The error type associated to this trait implementation.
186	    type Error: Into<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>;
187	
188	    /// Returns the maximum amount of tokens available for loan.
189	    ///
190	    /// NOTE: This function does not consider any form of supply cap, so in case
191	    /// it's used in a token with a cap like
192	    /// [`crate::token::erc20::extensions::Capped`], make sure to override this
193	    /// function to integrate the cap instead of [`U256::MAX`].
194	    ///
195	    /// # Arguments
196	    ///
197	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
198	    /// * `token` - The address of the token that is requested.
199	    #[must_use]
200	    fn max_flash_loan(&self, token: Address) -> U256;
201	
202	    /// Returns the fee applied when doing flash loans.
203	    ///
204	    /// # Arguments
205	    ///
206	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
207	    /// * `token` - The token to be flash loaned.
208	    /// * `value` - The amount of tokens to be loaned.
209	    ///
210	    /// # Errors
211	    ///
212	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedToken`] - If the token is not supported.
213	    ///
214	    /// # Examples
215	    ///
216	    /// ```rust,ignore
217	    /// fn flash_fee(&self, token: Address, value: U256) -> Result<U256, flash_mint::Error> {
218	    ///     self.erc20_flash_mint.flash_fee(token, value)
219	    /// }
220	    /// ```
221	    fn flash_fee(
222	        &self,
223	        token: Address,
224	        value: U256,
225	    ) -> Result<U256, Self::Error>;
226	
227	    /// Performs a flash loan.
228	    ///
229	    /// New tokens are minted and sent to the `receiver`, who is required to
230	    /// implement the [`IERC3156FlashBorrower`] interface. By the end of the
231	    /// flash loan, the receiver is expected to own value + fee tokens and have
232	    /// them approved back to the token contract itself so they can be burned.
233	    ///
234	    /// Returns a boolean value indicating whether the operation succeeded.
235	    ///
236	    /// # Arguments
237	    ///
238	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
239	    /// * `receiver` - The receiver of the flash loan. Should implement the
240	    ///   [`IERC3156FlashBorrower::on_flash_loan`] interface.
241	    /// * `token` - The token to be flash loaned. Only the address of this
242	    ///   contract (`self.vm().contract_address()`) is supported.
243	    /// * `value` - The amount of tokens to be loaned.
244	    /// * `data` - Arbitrary data that is passed to the receiver.
245	    ///
246	    /// # Errors
247	    ///
248	    /// * [`Error::ExceededMaxLoan`] - If the `value` is greater than the value
249	    ///   returned by [`IErc3156FlashLender::max_flash_loan`].
250	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedToken`] - If `token` is not supported.
251	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If the `token` address is not a contract
252	    ///   , the contract fails to execute the call, or the receiver does not
253	    ///   return [`BORROWER_CALLBACK_VALUE`].
254	    ///
255	    /// # Events
256	    ///
257	    /// * [`erc20::Transfer`].
258	    /// * [`erc20::Approval`].
259	    ///
260	    /// # Panics
261	    ///
262	    /// * If the new (temporary) total supply exceeds [`U256::MAX`].
263	    /// * If the sum of the loan value and fee exceeds the maximum value of
264	    ///   [`U256::MAX`].
265	    fn flash_loan(
266	        &mut self,
267	        receiver: Address,
268	        token: Address,
269	        value: U256,
270	        data: Bytes,
271	    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error>;
272	}
273	
274	impl Erc20FlashMint {
275	    /// See [`IErc3156FlashLender::max_flash_loan`].
276	    #[must_use]
277	    pub fn max_flash_loan(&self, token: Address, erc20: &erc20::Erc20) -> U256 {
278	        if token == self.vm().contract_address() {
279	            U256::MAX - erc20.total_supply()
280	        } else {
281	            U256::MIN
282	        }
283	    }
284	
285	    /// See [`IErc3156FlashLender::flash_fee`].
286	    #[allow(clippy::missing_errors_doc)]
287	    pub fn flash_fee(
288	        &self,
289	        token: Address,
290	        _value: U256,
291	    ) -> Result<U256, Error> {
292	        if token == self.vm().contract_address() {
293	            Ok(self.flash_fee_value.get())
294	        } else {
295	            Err(Error::UnsupportedToken(ERC3156UnsupportedToken { token }))
296	        }
297	    }
298	
299	    // This function can reenter, but it doesn't pose a risk because it always
300	    // preserves the property that the amount minted at the beginning is always
301	    // recovered and burned at the end, or else the entire function will revert.
302	    /// See [`IErc3156FlashLender::flash_loan`].
303	    #[allow(clippy::missing_panics_doc, clippy::missing_errors_doc)]
304	    pub fn flash_loan(
305	        &mut self,
306	        receiver: Address,
307	        token: Address,
308	        value: U256,
309	        data: &Bytes,
310	        erc20: &mut Erc20,
311	    ) -> Result<bool, Error> {
312	        let max_loan = self.max_flash_loan(token, erc20);
313	        if value > max_loan {
314	            return Err(Error::ExceededMaxLoan(ERC3156ExceededMaxLoan {
315	                max_loan,
316	            }));
317	        }
318	
319	        let fee = self.flash_fee(token, value)?;
320	        if !AddressUtils::has_code(self, receiver) {
321	            return Err(Error::ERC3156InvalidReceiver(
322	                ERC3156InvalidReceiver { receiver },
323	            ));
324	        }
325	        erc20._mint(receiver, value)?;
326	        let loan_receiver = IERC3156FlashBorrower::new(receiver);
327	        let call = Call::new_mutating(self);
328	        let loan_return = loan_receiver
329	            .on_flash_loan(
330	                self.vm(),
331	                call,
332	                self.vm().msg_sender(),
333	                token,
334	                value,
335	                fee,
336	                data.to_vec().into(),
337	            )
338	            .map_err(|_| {
339	                Error::ERC3156InvalidReceiver(ERC3156InvalidReceiver {
340	                    receiver,
341	                })
342	            })?;
343	        if loan_return != BORROWER_CALLBACK_VALUE {
344	            return Err(Error::ERC3156InvalidReceiver(
345	                ERC3156InvalidReceiver { receiver },
346	            ));
347	        }
348	
349	        let allowance = value
350	            .checked_add(fee)
351	            .expect("allowance should not exceed `U256::MAX`");
352	        erc20._spend_allowance(
353	            receiver,
354	            self.vm().contract_address(),
355	            allowance,
356	        )?;
357	
358	        let flash_fee_receiver = self.flash_fee_receiver_address.get();
359	
360	        if fee.is_zero() || flash_fee_receiver.is_zero() {
361	            erc20._burn(receiver, allowance)?;
362	        } else {
363	            erc20._burn(receiver, value)?;
364	            erc20._transfer(receiver, flash_fee_receiver, fee)?;
365	        }
366	
367	        Ok(true)
368	    }
369	}

1	//! ERC-4626 Tokenized Vault Standard Implementation as defined in [ERC-4626].
2	//!
3	//! This extension allows the minting and burning of "shares" (represented using
4	//! the ERC-20 inheritance) in exchange for underlying "assets" through
5	//! standardized `deposit`, `mint`, `redeem` and `burn` workflows. This contract
6	//! extends the ERC-20 standard. Any additional extensions included along it
7	//! would affect the "shares" token represented by this contract and not the
8	//! "assets" token which is an independent contract.
9	
10	use alloc::{vec, vec::Vec};
11	
12	use alloy_primitives::{uint, Address, U256, U8};
13	use openzeppelin_stylus_proc::interface_id;
14	pub use sol::*;
15	use stylus_sdk::{
16	    prelude::*,
17	    storage::{StorageAddress, StorageU8},
18	    stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError,
19	};
20	
21	use super::IErc20Metadata;
22	use crate::{
23	    token::erc20::{
24	        self,
25	        interface::{Erc20Interface, IErc20MetadataInterface},
26	        utils::{safe_erc20, ISafeErc20, SafeErc20},
27	        Erc20, IErc20,
28	    },
29	    utils::math::alloy::{Math, Rounding},
30	};
31	
32	const ONE: U256 = uint!(1_U256);
33	const TEN: U256 = uint!(10_U256);

36	mod sol {
37	    use alloy_sol_macro::sol;
38	
39	    sol! {
40	        /// Emitted when assets are deposited into the contract.
41	        #[derive(Debug)]
42	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
43	        event Deposit(address indexed sender, address indexed owner, uint256 assets, uint256 shares);
44	
45	        /// Emitted when assets are withdrawn from the contract.
46	        #[derive(Debug)]
47	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
48	        event Withdraw(
49	            address indexed sender,
50	            address indexed receiver,
51	            address indexed owner,
52	            uint256 assets,
53	            uint256 shares
54	        );
55	    }
56	
57	    sol! {
58	        /// Indicates an attempt to deposit more assets than the max amount for
59	        /// `receiver`.
60	        ///
61	        /// * `receiver` - Address of the asset's recipient.
62	        /// * `assets` - Amount of assets deposited.
63	        /// * `max` - Maximum amount of assets that can be deposited.
64	        #[derive(Debug)]
65	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
66	        error ERC4626ExceededMaxDeposit(address receiver, uint256 assets, uint256 max);
67	
68	        /// Indicates an attempt to mint more shares than the max amount for
69	        /// `receiver`.
70	        ///
71	        /// * `receiver` - Address of share's recipient.
72	        /// * `shares` - Amount of shares to mint.
73	        /// * `max` - Maximum amount of shares that can be minted.
74	        #[derive(Debug)]
75	        #[allow(missing_docs)]

1026	    ///   [`Address::ZERO`].
1027	    ///
1028	    /// # Events
1029	    ///

1031	    pub fn _deposit(
1032	        &mut self,
1033	        caller: Address,
1034	        receiver: Address,
1035	        assets: U256,
1036	        shares: U256,
1037	        erc20: &mut Erc20,
1038	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
1039	        // If asset() is ERC-777, `transfer_from` can trigger a reentrancy
1040	        // BEFORE the transfer happens through the `tokens_to_send` hook. On the
1041	        // other hand, the `token_received` hook, that is triggered after the
1042	        // transfer, calls the vault, which is assumed not malicious.
1043	        //
1044	        // Conclusion: we need to do the transfer before we mint so that any
1045	        // reentrancy would happen before the assets are transferred and before
1046	        // the shares are minted, which is a valid state.
1047	
1048	        self.safe_erc20.safe_transfer_from(
1049	            self.asset(),
1050	            caller,
1051	            self.vm().contract_address(),
1052	            assets,
1053	        )?;
1054	
1055	        erc20._mint(receiver, shares)?;
1056	
1057	        self.vm().log(Deposit {
1058	            sender: caller,
1059	            owner: receiver,
1060	            assets,

1093	        assets: U256,

1106	        // Conclusion: we need to do the transfer after the burn so that any

1110	        erc20._burn(owner, shares)?;
